patients.label: 46-year-old man with seizure-like episodes later diagnosed as pancreatic insulinoma

identity_evidence.quote: We present a case report of a 46-year-old man who started to experience seizure-like episodes.

attribution_limitations: Time of day of the seizures is described differently: the case section says they were predominantly linked to nighttime and at first appeared in the early morning hours, while the discussion says all seizures occurred at night. Each statement is kept where it is stated; the discussion wording is review_only.
The authors say they cannot exclude a milder degree of mental status alteration in the pre-ictal state, because the patient was clinically fully responsive but no detailed testing was performed.
The pre-ictal EEG is described as slow activity over both temporal regions in the case analysis and as diffuse slowing in the discussion; both statements are kept as authored.

The Figure 2B caption prints "At 1:49." as a separate fragment ending in a full stop, followed by the sentence describing violent rocking, squealing, hand flailing and loss of response; attaching 1:49 to that sentence reads the full stop as a print artefact.

claims.text: A 46-year-old man started to experience seizure-like episodes, predominantly at night and lasting tens of minutes. At first they appeared in the early morning hours as bizarre behavior with grunting, blowing, sitting up or rocking movements, and he was mainly unresponsive to verbal stimuli. Frequency rose to 4 to 5 per month and duration to 3 h.
